purpose: Diagnostic only: distinguish module/load-order, output-buffer and timing drift effects. This does not adopt a kernel or revise either earlier REJECT.
modules: control_a and control_b compile the exact same source path with equal-length extension names; candidate uses the recorded v2 source
group_design: All six module measurement permutations crossed with three output-pool rotations; every process contains all 18 combinations
correctness: Independent CPU float32 butterfly, storage rounding and INT4 oracle; all module/pool combinations checked before timing; inputs checked after each case
metrics: Raw synchronized wall time, process and current-thread CPU time per block; monotonic timestamps; per-process context-switch/page-fault and GC-collection deltas; optional CPU frequency. Record separate medians and within-group paired ratios/differences. These are diagnostic counters, not instruction-level attribution.
decision_rule: Report evidence by case/condition/process. A persistent difference requires the same direction beyond 5% in all three processes with matched control_a/control_b within 5%. Flag broad within-block variation separately. No automatic retry, no filtered samples and no production acceptance decision.
cpu: Pin each measuring process to the first allowed CPU; torch/OMP/OpenBLAS threads=1
shutdown: Recover all data and verify hashes before shutting down the instance
